spec.title: PodBay resource observation and interaction drivers

status.comment: Owner-approved resource contract. This document specifies behavior to implement; PB01 does not provide these capabilities.

p.ownership: The pod supervisor owns every declared process, PTY master, structured provider sidecar, and resource event source. Wayfinder, Zap, browser clients, and terminal viewers hold detachable client connections only. A resource has a stable ResourceId and an explicit incarnation bound to the pod and process identity. A stale handle cannot address a replacement process with the same operating-system PID or display name.

p.driver-boundary: The common pod and resource contract supplies identity, authority, command recording, observations, leases, budgets, and recovery. ProviderAdapter, TuiDriver, and the future BrowserDriver have distinct versioned commands, observations, and completion evidence. A successful API acknowledgement, PTY byte write, and browser click are not interchangeable outcomes. There is no untyped universal act operation.

p.pty-view: Every open PodBay PTY supports any authorized number of independent read-only viewers. Attaching returns resource identity, geometry, process observation, a consistent current-screen snapshot, fidelity, and a replay watermark. Subsequent output and resize events start strictly after that watermark. Closing a viewer never stops the pod, child process, or other viewers.

p.screen-state: A terminal-state projection retains the primary and alternate buffers, cursor, attributes, modes, geometry, decoder checkpoint, and source cursor needed to represent a full-screen application. A bounded byte tail alone is not a current-screen snapshot. Unsupported control sequences, missing output, decoder drift, or retention loss produce Partial or Unknown fidelity and an explicit gap. The renderer must not paint an inferred screen as a verified one.

p.output-order: Raw PTY output is retained as bytes with monotonic source positions; UTF-8 decoder state may cross chunks. Resize and other screen-affecting events are ordered with output. Snapshot projection and watermark correspond to the same committed state. A slow viewer cannot grow pod memory without bound; backpressure or explicit truncation preserves a truthful gap marker.

p.input-lease: Read access gives no input authority. A scoped, exclusive input lease binds the actor, ResourceId, incarnation, control epoch, and expiry. Write, paste, key, resize, and process-control commands require the appropriate current lease and grant. One controller determines the actual PTY size; other viewers adapt their own display. Human takeover advances the input epoch and fences pending automation before further human input. Disconnect or lease expiry does not resume an old keystroke sequence automatically.

p.input-outcome: A command has a durable logical ID, content digest, target incarnation, lease epoch, and bounded payload. Receipts distinguish recorded intent, bytes written, postcondition verified by a driver, rejected before write, and uncertain after a possible write. Written bytes cannot be cancelled retroactively. An unacknowledged or timed-out keystroke is never replayed blindly. Raw input and output may contain secrets and remain protected evidence rather than default public telemetry.

p.tui-driver: A TuiDriver profile names the supported application version/build, configuration or keymap, locale, TERM/encoding, geometry assumptions, parser version, typed actions, and their postconditions. Exact observed cells and bytes are separate from a recognized application state, an inferred hypothesis, and Ambiguous, Stale, or Unsupported states. A confidence score alone grants neither permission nor readiness. Unsupported semantic automation may coexist with fully functional authorized PTY viewing and raw input.

p.tui-action: A TUI action checks a fresh resource incarnation, screen revision, parser profile, grant, and input lease before a bounded step. It then observes a specific postcondition. Unexpected dialogs, output gaps, a changed layout, timeout after possible input, or human takeover stop the sequence with explicit uncertainty and require renewed observation. A prompt-looking screen is not a provider acknowledgement, permission grant, or proof of idle.

p.browser-driver: A future BrowserDriver uses the same pod-owned resource lifetime and authority ledger but separate browser-context, page, frame, navigation, DOM, locator, screenshot, download, and network-capability semantics. Any Playwright engine or helper is a declared pod-owned resource, not a second execution owner. A successful click is not proof that a requested business effect occurred. Browser-driver implementation is a later capability and is not part of the first PodBay readiness gate.

p.verification: Focused isolated fixtures must cover Midnight Commander and Vim navigation, a disposable file edit, primary and alternate screens, two viewers, snapshot-plus-replay, retention gaps, lease takeover, input/resize fencing, an unexpected modal, timeout after possible input, and manager restart while the same PTY process remains alive. Tests may launch fresh private fixture PTYs; they must not attach to a user's existing terminal or alter live work files. Future browser fixtures have their own capability and evidence gate.
